document.title: Dogfood helper: review current branch vs main
document.summary: `comprehende review` indexes live git and writes a covering skeleton. The next skill, README, and AGENTS.md start from that file instead of a hand-built review.json.
document.why: [#84](source:s1) asks for a CLI that writes hunk refs so agents stop pasting them. [Mate](source:s2) says that file is a skeleton: the skill still fills title, why, summary, groups, and lookFor.

sources.title: [Compre] Dogfood helper: review current branch vs main
sources.gist: Cloud agents paste hunk refs by hand. A CLI helper should write them from base...head.

sources.label: Mate on #84
sources.gist: The CLI must not invent a review. Stub prose only; the skill fills interpretation.
sources.author: matemolnar8
sources.body:
This is not a CLI that invents the review document. The LLM/skill still fills interpretation (title, why, summary, groups, lookFor, parts).

Suggested shape:
1. CLI indexes base...head and writes a skeleton review.json: every hunk ref present, minimal stubs only (or empty prose fields the skill must fill).
2. Agent/skill runs as today and fills the interpretation.
3. Optional: validate → serve/export after that.

Success metric: zero hand-pasted hunk refs; LLM still owns the meaning.

sources.label: PR #91
sources.gist: Adds comprehende review, a covering skeleton, and skill/docs that start from that file.

sources.label: Add a review command that writes a covering skeleton.
sources.gist: Indexes base...head and writes every hunk ref with stub prose only. Interpretation stays with the skill.

lookFor: [#84](source:s1) asked the helper to validate and optionally serve or export. `review` validates coverage after write and prints serve/export as next steps; it does not start a server.
[#84](source:s1) named `origin/main...HEAD`. Defaults match `index`: `origin/HEAD`, then main or master.
[Mate](source:s2) says the CLI must not invent a review. The skeleton title is `Untitled`, one `ungrouped` group, and no document why, lookFor, sources, or parts.
The published skill in `skills/comprehende/` is not released, so `npx skills add` still starts from `index`.

groups.title: Covering skeleton
groups.why: [#84](source:s1) needs every hunk ref in a file without inventing a review. [Mate](source:s2) names that file a skeleton.
groups.summary: `skeletonDocument` copies every index hunk into one `ungrouped` group with stub prose. `cmdReview` writes that JSON and validates coverage.

groups.title: review command
groups.why: Agents need a named command that writes the skeleton from cwd git.
groups.summary: `comprehende review` takes the same `--base`/`--head` as `index`, requires `--data`, writes the skeleton path, and prints fill then validate/serve/export.

groups.title: Skeleton coverage tests
groups.why: The success metric is every index hunk ref in the file, with no invented review prose.
groups.summary: Unit tests compare skeleton hunk refs to the index, reject missing `--data`, and the packed bin writes the same covering file.

groups.title: Skill starts from review
groups.why: Cloud agents follow the next skill. If it still says run `index` and paste refs, they will keep pasting.
groups.summary: The next skill writes a covering skeleton with `review --data`, then fills and splits groups from those refs.

groups.title: README and AGENTS
groups.why: [#84](source:s1) asks that cloud agents can find the helper in README or AGENTS.
groups.summary: README documents `comprehende review`. AGENTS.md tells PR dogfood to start from that skeleton.

groups.title: Installed next-skill copy
groups.why: `.agents/skills/comprehende` is a copy of `skills-next`. Tests fail if they drift.
groups.summary: `pnpm sync:skill` copies the new workflow and example into `.agents`.
